verses.zh: 犹大王亚哈斯十二年，以拉的儿子何细亚在撒马利亚登基作以色列王九年。
verses.en: In the twelfth year of King Ahaz’s reign over Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel. He reigned in Samaria[NOTE:1] for nine years.
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 他行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，只是不像在他以前的以色列诸王。
verses.en: He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord, but not to the same degree as the Israelite kings who preceded him.
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”

verses.zh: 亚述王撒缦以色上来攻击何细亚，何细亚就服事他，给他进贡。
verses.en: King Shalmaneser of Assyria marched up to attack[NOTE:1] him; so Hoshea became his subject and paid him tribute.
notes: Heb “went up against.”

verses.zh: 何细亚背叛，差人去见埃及王梭，不照往年所行的与亚述王进贡。亚述王知道了，就把他锁禁，囚在监里。
verses.en: The king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea was planning a revolt.[NOTE:1] Hoshea had sent messengers to King So[NOTE:2] of Egypt and had not sent his annual tribute to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria arrested him and imprisoned him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the king of Assyria found in Hoshea conspiracy.”
For discussion of this name, see HALOT 744 s.v. סוֹא and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 196.
Heb “and bound him in the house of confinement.”

verses.zh: 亚述王上来攻击以色列遍地，上到撒马利亚，围困三年。
verses.en: The king of Assyria marched through[NOTE:1] the whole land. He attacked Samaria and besieged it for three years.
notes: Heb “went up against.”

verses.zh: 何细亚第九年亚述王攻取了撒马利亚，将以色列人掳到亚述，把他们安置在哈腊与歌散的哈博河边，并米底亚人的城邑。
verses.en: In the ninth year of Hoshea’s reign, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported the people of Israel[NOTE:1] to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, along the Habor (the river of Gozan), and in the cities of the Medes.
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “Israel” as the object of the verb.

verses.zh: 这是因以色列人得罪那领他们出埃及地、脱离埃及王法老手的耶和华―他们的　神，去敬畏别神，
verses.en: This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from the land of Egypt and freed them from the power of[NOTE:1] Pharaoh king of Egypt. They worshiped[NOTE:2] other gods;
notes: Heb “and from under the hand of.” The words “freed them” for stylistic reasons replace the term “under.”
Heb “feared.”

verses.zh: 随从耶和华在他们面前所赶出外邦人的风俗和以色列诸王所立的条规。
verses.en: they observed the practices[NOTE:1] of the nations whom the Lord had driven out from before them,[NOTE:2] and followed the example of the kings of Israel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “walked in the customs.”
Heb “before the sons of Israel.”
Heb “and [the practices of] the kings of Israel which they did.”

verses.zh: 以色列人暗中行不正的事，违背耶和华―他们的　神，在他们所有的城邑，从了望楼直到坚固城，建筑邱坛；
verses.en: The Israelites said things about the Lord their God that were not right.[NOTE:1] They built high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.
notes: The meaning of the verb וַיְחַפְּאוּ (vayekhappeʾu), translated here “said,” is uncertain. Some relate it to the verbal root חָפַה (khafah), “to cover,” and translate “they did it in secret” (see BDB 341 s.v. חָפָא). However, the pagan practices specified in the following sentences were hardly done in secret. Others propose a meaning “ascribe, impute,” which makes good contextual sense but has little etymological support (see HALOT 339 s.v. חפא). In this case Israel claimed that the Lord authorized their pagan practices.

verses.zh: 在各高冈上、各青翠树下立柱像和木偶；
verses.en: They set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

verses.zh: 在邱坛上烧香，效法耶和华在他们面前赶出的外邦人所行的，又行恶事惹动耶和华的怒气；
verses.en: They burned incense on all the high places just like the nations whom the Lord had driven away before them did. Their evil practices made the Lord angry.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they did evil things, angering the Lord.”

verses.zh: 且事奉偶像，就是耶和华警戒他们不可行的。
verses.en: They worshiped[NOTE:1] the disgusting idols[NOTE:2] in blatant disregard of the Lord’s command.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “served.”
See the note at 1 Kgs 15:12.
Heb “about which the Lord had said to them, ‘You must not do this thing.’”

verses.zh: 但耶和华藉众先知、先见劝戒以色列人和犹大人说：「当离开你们的恶行，谨守我的诫命律例，遵行我吩咐你们列祖，并藉我仆人众先知所传给你们的律法。」
verses.en: The Lord solemnly warned Israel and Judah through all his prophets and all the seers, “Turn back from your evil ways; obey my commandments and rules that are recorded in the law. I ordered your ancestors to keep this law and sent my servants the prophets to remind you of its demands.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “obey my commandments and rules according to all the law which I commanded your fathers and which I sent to you by the hand of my servants the prophets.”

verses.zh: 他们却不听从，竟硬着颈项，效法他们列祖，不信服耶和华―他们的　神，
verses.en: But they did not pay attention and were as stubborn as their ancestors,[NOTE:1] who had not trusted the Lord their God.
notes: Heb and they stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers.”

verses.zh: 厌弃他的律例和他与他们列祖所立的约，并劝戒他们的话，随从虚无的神，自己成为虚妄，效法周围的外邦人，就是耶和华嘱咐他们不可效法的；
verses.en: They rejected his rules, the covenant he had made with their ancestors, and the laws he had commanded them to obey.[NOTE:1] They paid allegiance to[NOTE:2] worthless idols, and so became worthless to the Lord.[NOTE:3] They copied the practices of the surrounding nations in blatant disregard of the Lord’s command.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “and his warnings he had given them.”

Heb “They went [or, ‘followed’] after.” This idiom probably does not mean much if translated literally. It is found most often in Deuteronomy or in literature related to the covenant. It refers in the first instance to loyalty to God and to His covenant or His commandments (1 Kgs 14:8; 2 Chr 34:31) with the metaphor of a path or way underlying it (Deut 11:28; 28:14). To “follow other gods” was to abandon this way and this loyalty (to “abandon” or “forget” God, Judg 2:12; Hos 2:13) and to follow the customs or religious traditions of the pagan nations (2 Kgs 17:15). The classic text on “following” God or another god is 1 Kgs 18:18, 21 where Elijah taunts the people with “halting between two opinions” whether the Lord was the true God or Baal was. The idiom is often found followed by “to serve and to worship” or “they served and worshiped” such and such a god or entity (Jer 8:2; 11:10; 13:10; 16:11; 25:6; 35:15).

Heb “they followed after the worthless thing/things and became worthless.” The words “to the Lord” are not in the Hebrew text but are implicit from the context. There is an obvious wordplay on the verb “became worthless” and the noun “worthless thing”, which is probably to be understood collectively and to refer to idols as it does in Jer 8:19; 10:8; 14:22; Jonah 2:8.
Heb “and [they walked] after the nations which were around them, concerning which the Lord commanded them not to do like them.”

verses.zh: 离弃耶和华―他们　神的一切诫命，为自己铸了两个牛犊的像，立了亚舍拉，敬拜天上的万象，事奉巴力，
verses.en: They abandoned all the commandments of the Lord their God; they made two metal calves and an Asherah pole, bowed down to all the stars in the sky,[NOTE:1] and worshiped[NOTE:2] Baal.
notes: The phrase כָל צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם (khol tsevaʾ hashamayim), traditionally translated “all the host of heaven,” refers to the heavenly lights, including stars and planets. In 1 Kgs 22:19 these heavenly bodies are pictured as members of the Lord’s royal court or assembly, but many other texts view them as the illegitimate objects of pagan and Israelite worship.
Or “served.”

verses.zh: 又使他们的儿女经火，用占卜，行法术卖了自己，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，惹动他的怒气。
verses.en: They passed their sons and daughters through the fire,[NOTE:1] and practiced divination and omen reading. They committed themselves to doing evil in the sight of the Lord and made him angry.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note at 2 Kgs 16:3.
Heb “they sold themselves to doing what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, angering him.”

verses.zh: 所以耶和华向以色列人大大发怒，从自己面前赶出他们，只剩下犹大一个支派。
verses.en: So the Lord was furious[NOTE:1] with Israel and rejected them;[NOTE:2] only the tribe of Judah was left.
notes: Heb “very angry.”
Heb “turned them away from his face.”

verses.zh: 犹大人也不遵守耶和华―他们　神的诫命，随从以色列人所立的条规。
verses.en: Judah also failed to keep the commandments of the Lord their God; they followed Israel’s example.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they walked in the practices of Israel which they did.”

verses.zh: 耶和华就厌弃以色列全族，使他们受苦，把他们交在抢夺他们的人手中，以致赶出他们离开自己面前，
verses.en: So the Lord rejected all of Israel’s descendants; he humiliated[NOTE:1] them and handed them over to robbers, until he had thrown them from his presence.
notes: Or “afflicted.”

verses.zh: 将以色列国从大卫家夺回；他们就立尼八的儿子耶罗波安作王。耶罗波安引诱以色列人不随从耶和华，陷在大罪里。
verses.en: He tore Israel away from David’s dynasty, and Jeroboam son of Nebat became their king.[NOTE:1] Jeroboam drove Israel away[NOTE:2] from the Lord and encouraged them to commit a serious sin.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king.”
The consonantal text (Kethib) assumes the verb is נָדָא (nadaʾ), an alternate form of נָדָה (nadah), “push away.” The marginal reading (Qere) assumes the verb נָדָח (nadakh), “drive away.”
Heb “a great sin.”

verses.zh: 以色列人犯耶罗波安所犯的一切罪，总不离开，
verses.en: The Israelites followed in the sinful ways of Jeroboam and did not repudiate[NOTE:1] them.
notes: Heb “turn away from.”

verses.zh: 以致耶和华从自己面前赶出他们，正如藉他仆人众先知所说的。这样，以色列人从本地被掳到亚述，直到今日。
verses.en: Finally[NOTE:1] the Lord rejected Israel[NOTE:2] just as he had warned he would do[NOTE:3] through all his servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to Assyria and remains there to this very day.
notes: Heb “until.”
Heb “the Lord turned Israel away from his face.”
Heb “just as he said.”

verses.zh: 亚述王从巴比伦、古他、亚瓦、哈马，和西法瓦音迁移人来，安置在撒马利亚的城邑，代替以色列人；他们就得了撒马利亚，住在其中。
verses.en: The king of Assyria brought foreigners[NOTE:1] from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria[NOTE:2] in place of the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
notes: The object is supplied in the translation.
In vv. 24-29 Samaria stands for the entire northern kingdom of Israel.

verses.zh: 他们才住那里的时候，不敬畏耶和华，所以耶和华叫狮子进入他们中间，咬死了些人。
verses.en: When they first moved in,[NOTE:1] they did not worship[NOTE:2] the Lord. So the Lord sent lions among them and the lions were killing them.
notes: Heb “in the beginning of their living there.”
Heb “fear.”

verses.zh: 有人告诉亚述王说：「你所迁移安置在撒马利亚各城的那些民，不知道那地之神的规矩，所以那神叫狮子进入他们中间，咬死他们。」
verses.en: The king of Assyria was told,[NOTE:1] “The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the requirements of the God of the land, so he has sent lions among them. They are killing the people[NOTE:2] because they do not know the requirements of the God of the land.”
notes: Heb “and they said to the king of Assyria, saying.” The plural subject of the verb is indefinite.
Heb “Look, they are killing them.”

verses.zh: 亚述王就吩咐说：「叫所掳来的祭司回去一个，使他住在那里，将那地之神的规矩指教那些民。」
verses.en: So the king of Assyria ordered, “Take back one of the priests whom you[NOTE:1] deported from there. He must settle there and teach them the requirements of the God of the land.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The second plural subject may refer to the leaders of the Assyrian army. However, some prefer to read “whom I deported,” changing the verb to a first person singular form with a third masculine plural pronominal suffix. This reading has some support from Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses.

Heb “and let them go and let them live there, and let him teach them the requirements of the God of the land.” The two plural verbs seem inconsistent with the preceding and following contexts, where only one priest is sent back to Samaria. The singular has the support of Greek, Syriac, and Latin witnesses.

verses.zh: 于是有一个从撒马利亚掳去的祭司回来，住在伯特利，指教他们怎样敬畏耶和华。
verses.en: So one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria went back and settled in Bethel.[NOTE:1] He taught them how to worship[NOTE:2] the Lord.
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Heb “fear.”

verses.zh: 然而，各族之人在所住的城里各为自己制造神像，安置在撒马利亚人所造有邱坛的殿中。
verses.en: But each of these nations made[NOTE:1] its own gods and put them in the shrines on the high places that the people of Samaria[NOTE:2] had made. Each nation did this in the cities where they lived.
notes: The verb “make” refers to the production of idols. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 210-11.
Heb “Samaritans.” This refers to the Israelites who had been deported from the land.

verses.zh: 巴比伦人造疏割・比讷像；古他人造匿甲像；哈马人造亚示玛像；
verses.en: The people from Babylon made Sukkoth Benoth,[NOTE:1] the people from Cuth made Nergal,[NOTE:2] the people from Hamath made Ashima,[NOTE:3]
notes: No deity is known by the name Sukkoth Benoth in extant Mesopotamian literature. For speculation as to the identity of this deity, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 211.
Nergal was a Mesopotamian god of the underworld.
This deity is unknown in extra-biblical literature. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 211-12.

verses.zh: 亚瓦人造匿哈和他珥他像；西法瓦音人用火焚烧儿女，献给西法瓦音的神亚得米勒和亚拿米勒。
verses.en: the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak,[NOTE:1] and the Sepharvites burned their sons in the fire as an offering to Adrammelech and Anammelech,[NOTE:2] the gods of Sepharvaim.
notes: Nibhaz and Tartak were two Elamite deities. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 212.
Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of the Sepharvaim are unknown in extra-biblical literature. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 212.

verses.zh: 他们惧怕耶和华，也从他们中间立邱坛的祭司，为他们在有邱坛的殿中献祭。
verses.en: At the same time they worshiped[NOTE:1] the Lord. They appointed some of their own people to serve as priests in the shrines on the high places.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “feared.”
Heb “and they appointed for themselves from their whole people priests for the high places and they were serving for them in the house[s] of the high places.”

verses.zh: 他们又惧怕耶和华，又事奉自己的神，从何邦迁移，就随何邦的风俗。
verses.en: They were worshiping[NOTE:1] the Lord and at the same time serving their own gods in accordance with the practices of the nations from which they had been deported.
notes: Heb “fearing.”

verses.zh: 他们直到如今仍照先前的风俗去行，不专心敬畏耶和华，不全守自己的规矩、典章，也不遵守耶和华吩咐雅各后裔的律法、诫命。〈雅各，就是从前耶和华起名叫以色列的。〉
verses.en: To this very day they observe their earlier practices. They do not worship[NOTE:1] the Lord; they do not obey the rules, regulations, law, and commandments that the Lord gave[NOTE:2] the descendants of Jacob, whom he renamed Israel.
notes: Heb “fear.”
Heb “commanded.”

verses.zh: 耶和华曾与他们立约，嘱咐他们说：「不可敬畏别神，不可跪拜事奉他，也不可向他献祭。
verses.en: The Lord made a covenant with them[NOTE:1] and instructed them, “You must not worship other gods. Do not bow down to them, serve them, or offer sacrifices to them.
notes: That is, the descendants of Jacob/Israel (see v. 35b).

verses.zh: 但那用大能和伸出来的膀臂领你们出埃及地的耶和华，你们当敬畏，跪拜，向他献祭。
verses.en: Instead you must worship the Lord, who brought you up from the land of Egypt by his great power and military ability;[NOTE:1] bow down to him and offer sacrifices to him.
notes: Heb “and outstretched arm.”

verses.zh: 他给你们写的律例、典章、律法、诫命，你们应当永远谨守遵行，不可敬畏别神。
verses.en: You must carefully obey at all times the rules, regulations, law, and commandments he wrote down for you. You must not worship other gods.

verses.zh: 我―耶和华与你们所立的约你们不可忘记，也不可敬畏别神。
verses.en: You must never forget the covenant I made with you, and you must not worship other gods.

verses.zh: 但要敬畏耶和华―你们的　神，他必救你们脱离一切仇敌的手。」
verses.en: Instead you must worship the Lord your God; then he will rescue you from the power of all your enemies.”

verses.zh: 他们却不听从，仍照先前的风俗去行。
verses.en: But they[NOTE:1] paid no attention; instead they observed their earlier practices.
notes: This refers to the foreigners whom the king of Assyria settled in the land (see v. 35a).

verses.zh: 如此这些民又惧怕耶和华，又事奉他们的偶像。他们子子孙孙也都照样行，效法他们的祖宗，直到今日。
verses.en: These nations were worshiping the Lord and at the same time serving their idols; their sons and grandsons are doing just as their fathers have done, to this very day.
